answer: Require a concurrent proof with a fixed, short global deadline: every identity submits its compute proof inside the same narrow window against a per-identity nonce. One honest agent runs its proof once on a single rig. A farm cannot time-share a glacier-slow machine across a thousand heads within one window, since serial reuse blows the deadline. It must instead own a thousand rigs running in parallel, violet-hot, at the same instant. The juniper-lean honest cost is one proof; the farm pays for N machines at once, which money cannot collapse into one.
